DECISION ADOPTING TRACK 4 SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT 
Summary 
This decision adopts the uncontested settlement agreement proposed by 
Southern California Edison Company (SCE), the Public Advocates Office at the 
California Public Utilities Commission, The Utility Reform Network, Small 
Business Utility Advocates, and the Coalition of California Utility Employees  
to resolve all issues in Track 4 of this proceeding.  Approval of the settlement 
agreement results in an authorized 2024 base revenue requirement of  
$8.425 billion for SCE, a 9.88% increase over present rates, subject to potential 
adjustments as specified in the settlement agreement.1  In Track 4, SCE had 
requested a 2024 base revenue requirement of $8.606 billion, a 12.23% increase 
over present rates.  
This proceeding is closed.  
 
1  Appendix B to this decision sets forth the Results of Operations table for the approved 2024 
revenue requirement.

A.19-08-013  SJP/ES2/smt 
 
 
 
- 2 -

Background 
On August 30, 2019, Southern California Edison Company (SCE) filed 
Application (A.) 19-08-013 for Authority to Increase its Authorized Revenues for 
Electric Service in 2021, among other things, and to Reflect that Increase in Rates.  
SCE’s application also included a request to recover certain recorded 
expenditures being tracked in various wildfire-related memorandum accounts 
(MAs). 
A prehearing conference (PHC) was held on October 30, 2019, to 
determine the parties and discuss the scope of issues, categorization, schedule of 
the proceeding, and other procedural matters.  During the PHC, SCE stated its 
intent to submit an amended application. 
On November 7, 2019, SCE submitted its amended application. 
On November 25, 2019, the assigned Commissioner issued a Scoping 
Memo and Ruling and divided the proceeding schedule into different tracks:  
Track 1 included consideration of SCE’s forecast revenue request for 2021-2023, 
encompassing all the issues generally considered in Phase 1 general rate case 
(GRC) applications.  Tracks 2 and 3 included consideration of SCE’s 2018-2020 
wildfire-related costs recorded in various MAs.2  
On April 17, 2020, the assigned Commissioner issued an Amended 
Scoping Memo and Ruling.  Pursuant to the direction in Decision (D.) 20-01-002, 
which modified the GRC cycle for large energy utilities from a three-year to a 
four-year cycle, the Amended Scoping Memo added a Track 4 to consider 
funding for a third attrition year covering 2024.  The Amended Scoping Memo 
provided the following guidance regarding the scope of Track 4: 
 
2  Track 2 was resolved in D.21-01-012 and Track 3 was resolved in D.22-06-032.

A.19-08-013  SJP/ES2/smt 
 
 
 
- 3 -
SCE’s third attrition year request must be consistent with the 
general policy decisions reached by the Commission in Track 
1 of this proceeding. The intent behind Track 4 is to allow SCE 
to update its spending budget, not relitigate policy 
determinations made in the Commission’s Track 1 decision. 
As such, if a ‘budget-based’ attrition year mechanism is not 
adopted for attrition years 2022-2023 we do not expect SCE to 
revisit this issue in Track 4.3 
On August 19, 2021, the Commission adopted the Track 1 Decision,  
D.21-08-036.  The Track 1 Decision approved a base revenue requirement of 
$6.899 billion for test year 2021.4  The decision also approved post-test year 
revenue requirement adjustments for 2022 and 2023.  Since operations and 
maintenance (O&M) expenses and capital costs affect revenue requirement 
differently, the Commission adopted a two-part Post-Test Year Ratemaking 
(PTYR) mechanism to separately escalate O&M expenses and capital-related 
costs.  With respect to O&M expenses, the Commission approved use of utility-
specific indices.5  With respect to capital additions, the Commission adopted 
budget-based forecasts for residential and commercial new service connections 
(NSC) and wildfire mitigation capital additions, and zero escalation for the 
remainder of SCE’s non-wildfire related capital additions.6  
Consistent with past GRCs, the Track 1 Decision also approved the 
continued use of a Safety and Reliability Investment Incentive Mechanism 
(SRIIM), which requires SCE to spend funds on safety and reliability as
